minutes.headline: ZBA, with one member recused, granted a special permit for a duplex on a lot with excess wetlands and short width.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard Phil Coletta's request for a special permit for dimensional variation to build a duplex at 1207 Mass Ave. The lot has more wetlands than the 10% the bylaw allows, and it is narrower than required. Members were split on the wetlands overage, and residents spoke in support. A motion to approve both reliefs was made and seconded, and the chair announced the permit granted after a voice vote.

public_comment.stated_role: speaking for his sister, the owner
public_comment.topic: Asked how the lot lost grandfathering when it never left the family. Noted the wetlands are in the rear corner and that the sewer stub implied a buildable lot.

public_comment.stated_role: Conservation Commission member, speaking as a private individual
public_comment.topic: Urged the board to grant the permit. Cited the sewer stub, driveway cut and taxes paid as a building lot.
Said the lot was listed as developable based on town records, with taxes and sewer betterment paid. Cited the family's hardship settling the estate and smaller lots built elsewhere.
Questioned why a sewer betterment was assessed from 2005 if the lot was not buildable. Asked whether the wet year affected the wetlands count and cited other small lots built.

votes.motion: Approve the request for a special permit for dimensional variation: relief on wetlands and 50 ft on lot width.
votes.moved_by: a board member (not named in captions)

budget_items.what_was_said: Applicant and speakers said the sewer stub is paid for and the lot is taxed as buildable. A later speaker said the betterment began in 2005.

decisions.decision: Applicant agreed to proceed with only four members able to vote, requiring a unanimous majority.
Chair read the permit conditions, including compliance with all other agencies, periodic review, a 14-day filing with the town clerk, and a two-year lapse unless construction begins.
The board noted that, if approved, the project must still go to the Conservation Commission.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a special permit for a duplex at 1207 Mass Ave, with relief on wetlands coverage and lot width, by voice vote.
The vote was taken with one member recused and only four members able to vote, which the applicant accepted, requiring a unanimous majority.
The board was split on the wetlands overage before the motion; residents spoke in support, citing the paid sewer stub and taxes assessed on the lot as buildable.
The chair read conditions including review by other agencies, a 14-day filing with the town clerk, and a two-year lapse unless construction begins.
The board noted the project must still go to the Conservation Commission.

why_it_matters: The permit relaxes two lot standards the bylaw sets, wetlands share and width, so it bears on how strictly the town applies them to other small, older lots.

The lot's tax and sewer betterment history was argued as evidence of buildability, which touches how residents' assessments and past charges are read when a lot is later found not to meet current rules.
watch_next: Conservation Commission review of the project, which the board said is still required.
Filing of the decision with the town clerk within 14 days, and whether construction begins before the two-year lapse.
